runtime_initialization_failure_containme.source: Jolt/Core/HashTable.h::GrowTable, lines 181-220 at the pinned source
runtime_initialization_failure_containme.finding: GrowTable moves old allocation pointers into locals and clears members before allocating replacement storage. If that allocation throws, old storage can become unreachable from the table.
runtime_initialization_failure_containme.behavior: The standalone owner releases reachable Factory maps, default material and Factory storage with the checked allocator hooks still installed, restores the initially-null hooks, and poisons the lifecycle owner. Initial ordinary null allocation reports AllocationFailure; subsequent acquisitions report InternalError and require process restart.
runtime_initialization_failure_containme.limitation: This does not establish strong exception safety or complete reclamation for all Jolt internal OOM paths. Registry/internal allocation sizes are not exactly instrumented by the per-world byte budget.
